relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - triggersAlert. Captures that Events and Alerts are not two independent catalogs but a superset/subset pair: every Critical or Warning severity event also surfaces as an Alert, while Info-severity events do not. No existing predicate in the registry expresses this event-to-alert escalation relationship.
relations.evidence: For events with the Critical and Warning severity, Capella sends an alert when the event occurs.

relations.subject: monitoring:event
relations.evidence: Capella writes all events to the [Activity Log](../clusters/monitoring/activity-log.md), where you can view them.

cross_component_finding: The event catalog itself (roughly 90 named events tagged with Resource: cluster/tenant/project/app services, and free-text Tags like security/billing/maintenance/performance) is a flat enumeration with no version-, edition-, or provider-gating language anywhere in the table - every event is unconditionally available. This is a clean confirmation of the batch hypothesis: a reference table of this shape (event catalog) carries essentially no ontology beyond the one escalation relationship to monitoring:alert already captured. Notably, several events explicitly mention AWS-specific behavior in free text ('Cluster Storage Not Increased... due to AWS limits on how often a volume can be modified') - this is a real within-Capella AWS-specific behavior difference (a storage-scaling operation that can fail specifically because of an AWS platform limit), which supports the same finding independently reached on aws.md/azure.md/gcp.md about disk auto-expansion/storage behavior varying by underlying cloud provider.
